heroHeadline: Chavismo Fractures Publicly as Rodríguez Shifts Toward Washington; Investors Return but Economy Lags
heroSubtitle: Venezuela's ruling Chavismo movement experienced its deepest public split in 27 years on June 1, as hardliner Interior Minister Diosdado Cabello and Defense Minister Padrino López openly challenged Acting President Delcy Rodríguez's pro-US normalization course — triggered by the May 17 deportation of Alex Saab to American courts and the May 23 US Marines exercise over Caracas. While US investors and American Airlines flights have returned to the capital, a Washington Post and PBS investigation on June 3 found that ordinary Venezuelans — still facing 612% annual inflation and a $5–10 monthly minimum wage — have seen little of the promised economic recovery. A June 2 HRW report highlighted a potential new accountability pathway through universal jurisdiction as Spain processes Argentina's extradition request for a Venezuelan security officer facing crimes against humanity charges. María Corina Machado continues pushing for election negotiations while the Rodríguez government has resisted setting a date, and approximately 800 political prisoners remain detained.
